sections.h2: Dholera's 50 MLD plant has three to five times one fab's water need

chart.title: Dholera's 50 MLD plant has three to five times one fab's estimated need
chart.sub: Ultrapure water capacity and estimated need, million litres a day (MLD).
chart.source: Dholera and Tata Electronics reporting, as cited in the post.

sections.means: The 50 MLD plant has three to five times the 10 to 15 MLD one mature-node fab is estimated to need, so the margin is real for one fab.
sections.todo: Re-run this comparison if Dholera adds a second fab or moves to more advanced nodes.

sections.h2: TSMC alone uses about 60% of Taiwan's chip-industry water

chart.title: TSMC's 150,000 tonnes a day is most of the industry's 250,000 total
chart.source: Taiwan water usage figures, as cited in the post.

sections.means: TSMC's 150,000 tonnes a day is about 60% of the 250,000 tonnes the whole Taiwan semiconductor industry uses, so one company drives most of the demand.
sections.todo: Update this share as usage grows, since the 2019 share figure is now several years old.

sections.h2: Taiwan's answer is dedicated reclaimed water, rising to 36,000 m³ a day by 2026

chart.title: Hsinchu's reclaimed-water plan rises from 10,000 to 36,000 m³ a day
chart.sub: Planned reclaimed-water supply at the Hsinchu Science Park plant, cubic metres a day.
chart.source: TSMC plant plans, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Taiwan responded with dedicated reclaimed-water plants, with Hsinchu's planned supply rising from 10,000 to 36,000 m³ a day by 2026.
sections.todo: Build reclaimed-water supply and a recycling-rate target alongside any new fab, as TSMC's 90.3% recycling rate shows.
